newsitem.title: MEXICO: Cuba official repeats 96-97 sugar crop outlook.
newsitem.headline: Cuba official repeats 96-97 sugar crop outlook.

text.p: Cuba's sugar harvest in this 1996-1997 campaign will end slightly above the 4.45 million tonnes produced in the previous cycle, a top official said here Wednesday.

"We do not have an extact figure but it will certainly be above, slightly more than last year," Cubaazucar vice-president Iris Nocedo de Leon told reporters here at the F.O. Licht World Sugar and Sweetners' Conference.
"The crop is going and that is the most important thing," Nocedo de Leon said about the current cycle, which in early March had hit the 2.0 million tonne mark.

Experts Cuba believe could reap 4.7 or 4.8 million tonnes this cycle because of increased fertilizer use and better crop care. Cuba's harvest dipped to a low of 3.3 million tonnes in 1994- 1995. For the upcoming 1997-1998 harvest, she said she had no figure to hand but that work was being done to "make a good recovery".
When asked what she thought of an analyst's view that Cuba could aim for a feasible goal of 6-6.5 million tonnes per harvest, she said Cuba had no target in such terms. "But it is possible."
"We are very flexible, we have to be very pragmatic. We need to recover with a cost efficiency," she said.
